Q1: This chemical presents known GHS Tier 1 hazards for carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, and reproductive toxicity (CMR), oral toxicity (ORL), and organ/systemic toxicity (OGN). It also has expanded Tier 2 perspectives for inhalation (IHL) and dermal/eye (SKN) hazards. However, there are significant data deficiencies (Tier 4) for environmental (ENV) and endocrine disruption (EDC) hazards.
Q2: Cupferron is listed on California's Proposition 65 as a chemical known to cause cancer, birth defects, or other reproductive harm. It is also identified by the International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC) as Group 2B, meaning it is possibly carcinogenic to humans.
Q3: With 1,650 literature references and 30 toxicity value records, Cupferron is moderately well-studied within our dataset, possessing a defined molecular structure. Despite this, it has not undergone the rigorous evaluation of EPA's IRIS or PPRTV programs, and significant data gaps exist for its environmental and endocrine disruption hazards.
